qs.q: A neonate born in a remote rural clinic presents with stunted growth, severe intellectual disability, a coarse face, and a protruding tongue due to congenital iodine deficiency. What is the precise endocrinological term for this condition?
o: Cretinism caused by congenital deficiency of thyroid hormone
Myxedema coma resulting from severe untreated adult hypothyroidism
Graves disease triggered by thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin
Primary hyperparathyroidism caused by a functional adenoma
qs.e: Cretinism is severe hypothyroidism present from birth or early infancy, usually caused by maternal iodine deficiency or thyroid absence, leading to characteristic developmental defects. Myxedema coma represents severe hypothyroidism in adults.

qs.q: An adult patient presents with severe intellectual disability, short stature and a coarse facial appearance, and a history of maternal iodine deficiency during pregnancy. Which factor most directly explains his condition?
o: Autoimmune destruction of the thyroid gland
Iodine deficiency in the mother leading to fetal hypothyroidism
Dyshormonogenesis due to thyroid enzyme defect
qs.e: Maternal iodine deficiency causes fetal hypothyroidism, producing the features described. Autoimmune thyroiditis and dyshormonogenesis are other causes but not linked to maternal iodine status.

qs.q: What is the primary underlying cause of an endemic goiter in patients experiencing iodine deficiency?
o: Autoimmune destruction of thyroid follicular cells
Benign localized tumor growth within the gland
Constant TSH stimulation causing glandular enlargement
qs.e: Iodine deficiency leads to endemic goiter as the thyroid gland enlarges under constant TSH stimulation to capture trace iodine. Autoimmune destruction is characteristic of Hashimoto's disease rather than simple dietary deficiency.

qs.q: Iodine deficiency goiter causes thyroid enlargement because
o: Iodine directly stimulates thyroid follicular cell proliferation.
Autoantibodies activate TSH receptors, leading to gland enlargement.
Reduced T3/T4 levels raise TSH, causing follicular hyperplasia and hypertrophy.
Decreased calcitonin production triggers thyroid cell proliferation.
qs.e: Most common cause of goiter worldwide = iodine deficiency. Treatment: iodine supplementation. Endemic goiter = affects >10% of a population.
